rationale: Clean-room WebGL port written from the one-line effect description only (no upstream source read): a dependency-free, domain-warped two-tone shader surface with faint contour lines gives hero panels and cards a living, technical backdrop, with a static CSS gradient when WebGL is unavailable.

colorA.description: First surface colour, as #rgb or #rrggbb; also tints the CSS fallback gradient.

colorB.description: Second surface colour, as #rgb or #rrggbb; also tints the CSS fallback gradient.

speed.description: Flow speed; 0 holds a still frame.

scale.description: Pattern scale; larger gives finer detail.

lines.description: Strength of the contour lines traced over the field.

grain.description: Film-grain amount, which also hides gradient banding.

interactive.description: Let the pointer gently pull the warp field toward it.

a11y: The injected canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; the host's content, reading order and focus behaviour are unchanged.
Pointer tracking is passive and decorative: no click, key or focus handling is added, and nothing depends on hovering.
The surface mixes bright and dark regions, so text on it should carry a shadow or scrim to keep 4.5:1 contrast (the demo does this).
Reduced motion stops the shader loop, the pointer pull and the fallback drift and shows one still frame; forced-colors mode hides the canvas and paints the host in Canvas/CanvasText.
